stem: In a certain code language, STAR is written as TCVU and FARM is written as OTCH. Using the same rule, how will GOLD be written in that code?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Reversing GOLD to DLOG and shifting each letter by +1 instead of +2 gives D+1=E, L+1=M, O+1=P, G+1=H = EMPH, applying the wrong shift magnitude.
The rule is: reverse the word, then shift each letter forward by 2. GOLD reversed is DLOG. D+2=F, L+2=N, O+2=Q, G+2=I. Answer: FNQI.
Reversing GOLD to DLOG and shifting each letter by +3 instead of +2 gives D+3=G, L+3=O, O+3=R, G+3=J = GORJ, applying an inflated shift.
Applying shift +2 to GOLD without reversing first gives G+2=I, O+2=Q, L+2=N, D+2=F = IQNF, omitting the reversal step.

explanation: The rule has two steps: (1) reverse the word, (2) shift each letter forward by 2. Verify with STAR: reversed = RATS; R+2=T, A+2=C, T+2=V, S+2=U -> TCVU (matches). Verify with FARM: reversed = MRAF; M+2=O, R+2=T, A+2=C, F+2=H -> OTCH (matches). Apply to GOLD: reversed = DLOG; D+2=F, L+2=N, O+2=Q, G+2=I -> FNQI.

explanation_sections.punchline: The two-step rule (reverse then shift +2) is detected by noticing the code letters do not match any direct shift of the original word - the reversal must come first.
explanation_sections.approach: Apply clues most-certain-first: test if STAR->TCVU is a direct shift - S+3=V not T, so direct shift fails. Test reversal: RATS shifted +2 = TCVU (works). Confirm on FARM: MRAF+2 = OTCH (works). Apply to GOLD: DLOG+2 = FNQI.
explanation_sections.lesson: When a direct letter-shift fails on the first example, test whether reversing the word first and then shifting resolves the pattern - this is the standard two-step coding trap.
explanation_sections.timing: 40 seconds. Two rule-hypothesis tests (direct shift fails, reverse-then-shift works), confirm on second example, apply. Trap: forgetting reversal (gives IQNF) or correct reversal but wrong shift magnitude.
